extract.description: Pull parts out of a web page with CSS selectors: a headline, a price, every link, or a list of products with a name and price each. Give it the page's address, or the HTML an earlier step fetched.
extract.name: extract

parameters.description: The page to read: its address, such as https://example.com/pricing, or what an earlier step fetched, such as @response from an HTTP step (links then come back in full) or an email's HTML body.
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: What to pull out of the page, each with a name and a CSS selector, as a browser's developer tools show it: h1, .price, #summary, a.next, table tr.
parameters.name: parts

all.description: Take every match, as a list, rather than the first one.

attribute.description: Take an attribute's value instead of the text: href for a link's address, src for an image's. Addresses come back in full.

html.description: Keep the HTML inside the element rather than its text.

name.description: What to call this part in the result, such as title or price.

selector.description: A CSS selector that finds it: h1, .price, #summary, a.next, img.hero, table tr. Leave empty for the whole page, or the whole item.

parameters.description: To read a list of things, a CSS selector for each of them, such as .product, article or table tr. The parts are then read inside each one, and the result is a list of records, one per match.
parameters.name: each

returns.description: What was pulled out. Each part is in 'parts' under its name (parts.price). With a List of, 'items' has one record per thing found, each with the parts under their names: loop over items, or read parts for the first one.

count.description: How many items were found. 1 without a List of.

items.description: With a List of, one record per thing found, each with the parts under their names, in page order. Otherwise a one-item list holding parts.

parts.description: Each part under its name: its text (or HTML, or the attribute asked for), a list of them when the part takes every match, or blank (null) when nothing matched. With a List of, the first item's parts.

url.description: The page's address, when it was fetched or came with one. Otherwise empty.

from_text.description: Turn Markdown or plain text into HTML for an email or a web page: headings, bold, lists, links and tables, with styles that email apps show. What an AI step writes in Markdown reads as it should.

mock_response.html:
Weekly summary

Three new customers signed up, and Acme upgraded to Pro.
mock_response.text:
Weekly summary

Three new customers signed up, and Acme upgraded to Pro.

from_text.name: from_text

parameters.description: What to turn into HTML, written in Markdown (# Heading, **bold**, - list items, [links](https://…), | tables) or as plain text, where each line break is kept. HTML passes through as it is.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Styled for an email, with the styles written into the HTML so every email app shows them, or plain, with no styles, for a web page or a template that has its own.
parameters.name: style

returns.description: The HTML, in 'html', ready for an email's body, and the same words as plain text in 'text'.

examples.html:
Weekly summary

Three new customers signed up, and Acme upgraded to Pro.
examples.text:
Weekly summary

Three new customers signed up, and Acme upgraded to Pro.

text.description: The same words as plain text, for an email's text-only version or a preview.

table.description: Turn rows into an HTML table that looks right in an email: the rows of a sheet, or any records an earlier step returned, with a column per field.
table.name: table

parameters.description: The rows, such as the rows a sheet or an earlier step returned. Each row's fields become the columns, named after them.
parameters.name: rows

parameters.description: The columns to show, in order, by field name, such as Name and Email. Leave empty for every field, in the order they first appear.
parameters.name: columns

parameters.description: A title shown above the table, such as This week's signups. Leave empty for none.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: Styled for an email, with the styles written into the HTML so every email app shows them, or plain, with no styles, for a web page or a template that has its own.
parameters.name: style

returns.description: The table as HTML, in 'html': put it in an email's body, on its own or inside other HTML.

count.description: How many rows the table has.

html.description: The table's HTML: a header row, then a row per record.

description: Pull parts out of a web page with CSS selectors, and build HTML such as a table for an email.
